speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn with yellowish discoloration of the skin; this is likely jaundice. To determine the cause and severity, how many days old are you, and is this yellowing spreading to your arms or legs?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-day-old male newborn. The newborn's mother reports that her child has developed yellowish discoloration of the skin that started from the face and then spread to the trunk since the past day. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination. The baby was born full-term at 38 weeks’ gestation via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding-associated (physiologic) jaundice.
Based on your history of exclusive breastfeeding every 2–3 hours and the pattern of jaundice spreading from the face to the trunk after day 5, this is a common and benign condition. We do not need further imaging or extensive testing at this time.
